newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey gives up on Bulgarian Turks deportation.
newsitem.headline: Turkey gives up on Bulgarian Turks deportation.

text.p: Turkish Defence Minister Turhan Tayan told parliament on Tuesday that the government had scrapped the planned expulsion of tens of thousands of Bulgarian ethnic Turks living in Turkey.

"Our government has decided to give residence permits to our ethnic kin of Bulgarian origin...this has been decided. Definitely nobody will be sent abroad and citizenship rights will be given," Tayan said.
An interior ministry official said last week the government had sent a directive that ordered local governors to expel around 70,000 Bulgarians whose visas had expired.
The order angered opposition political parties.
Turkey began giving citizenship to ethnic Turks, many of whom had fled forced assimilation in Bulgaria in the mid-1980s, in 1989.
But Turks kept migrating for economic reasons after Turco-Bulgarian relations improved and automatic citizenship was halted in 1993.
